items.title: 14 states agree to raise judicial officers' retirement age to 62 yrs: SC
items.summary:
The Supreme Court on Monday expressed satisfaction that as many as 14 states have agreed to raise the retirement age of district judicial officers from 60 to 62 years and refused to list for urgent hearing the separate pleas of judges who are on the verge of retiring or have just retired.
"This pertains to the persuasive jurisdiction of this court. The issue is between the Supreme Court and the states," a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said while declining to list individual pleas of judges who have to demit office after reaching the age of 60 years.
The CJI said that so far 14 states have agreed to raise the retirement age to 62 years and "we are hopeful that others will also follow." The bench said though it has listed the petition for hearing, it did not approve the moving of individual pleas by judicial officers.
Senior advocate Ranjit Kumar mentioned the plea for listing saying that judicial officers are retiring every day.

The 28-year-old had suffered a right adductor strain during the series-opener last week.
"Ishan is doing well. He will be training today. For tomorrow, I think he is not available for selection, just as a precaution," Morkel said at the pre-match press conference here.
Right adductor is a group of muscles located on the inner side of the thigh.
Kishan had missed the second T20I as well, with teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi replacing him in the playing XI.
Uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra was added to the squad as cover for Kishan. India lead the five-match series 2-0.

items.title: Trump names 2028 US election contenders
items.summary: Michigan: US President Donald Trump, offering an early glimpse into the Republican Party's political future, named JD Vance and Marco Rubio among the prominent figures who could run for the White House in 2028, boasting that the GOP possesses a "great bench" compared to the Democrats.In an interview with FOX 2's Roop Raj ahead of Michigan rally, when asked directly about who might launch a presidential bid in 2028, Trump stated that while it is premature to name an outright front-runner, the party has no shortage of strong candidates."I could tell you who I think, but it's a little bit early," Trump said."We have great names - you have JD Vance, Marco Rubio, and many others. We have a great bench; they (Democrats) have no bench," Trump said.Earlier while leaving for Michigan rally, Trump while interacting with the media, also touched upon geopolitical and energy challenges stemming from the Russia-Ukraine war, reiterating that Washington would not allow global energy security to be compromised by the ongoing conflict."We're not going to be hostage with the oil industry over something that, frankly, should've never started," Trump asserted, reiterating his stance that the war was preventable.Meanwhile, the November 3 midterm elections are shaping up as a crucial contest for control of both chambers of Congress. The outcome will have significant implications for Trump's legislative agenda and the balance of political power in Washington.United States midterm elections are nationwide votes held every four years at the exact midpoint of a president's term. Acting as a major political temperature check for the country, these elections determine control of the federal government by putting all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and about one-third of the Senate up for grabs.The political contest comes amid broader challenges for the administration, including economic concerns and declining approval ratings. The Wall Street Journal reported in September that Trump's approval rating had fallen to 37 per cent in its polling, a low for a president heading into midterm elections in the publication's polling history dating back to 1990.

items.title: Serbia's Vucic loses election after 14 years amid student-led protests

items.title: Serbia election: Vucic faces tough challenge from student-backed movement
items.summary:
Serbians are voting Sunday in a parliamentary election that is seen as a showdown between the Balkan country's populist leader Aleksandar Vucic and a movement of university students who led protests against him for almost two years.
Though Serbia's 6.4 million voters get to choose from 18 parties hoping to enter the 250-member Parliament, the election has taken shaped as a referendum between Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party and the youth-backed Students' List.
The main contenders are believed to be polling neck-and-neck, making Sunday's election the most uncertain in recent years. Turnout is expected to be high and could push most smaller parties below the 3% threshold needed to make it into the assembly.
While Vucic has routinely outplayed Serbia's fractured opposition in the past, the leaderless youth movement has proved to be a tough opponent that rattled his firm grip on power in Serbia like no one else could in the past 14 years since his party took office.

items.title: MCA extends annual filing deadlines
items.summary: New Delhi: The corporate affairs ministry has extended the deadline for companies to file their annual financial statements for the fiscal 2025-26 till December 31.Besides, companies can submit their annual returns to the ministry till January 31, 2027, as per a circular.The extension of deadlines follow representations from stakeholders as they were facing issues in submitting the annual statutory filings through the MCA 21 portal.According to the circular dated October 24, the ministry said that in view of the representations received and to enable companies to complete their annual statutory filings, the deadlines have been extended without paying an additional fee.Now, the annual financial statements in e-forms AOC-4, AOC-4 (CFS), AOC-4 (XBRL), AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS) and AOC-4 CFS NBFC (Ind AS) for the financial year 2025-26 can be filed up to December 31, 2026.For the 2025-26 fiscal year, annual returns in e-forms MGT-7 and MGT-7A can be submitted till January 31, 2027.Generally, the annual financial statements have to be submitted within 30 days of completing the Annual General Meetings (AGMs) and in the case of annual returns, the time period is 60 days.Prior to issuance of the circular, the deadlines for submitting annual financial statements and annual financial returns for 2025-26 fiscal was October 31 and November 30, 2026, respectively.The ministry also said the circular "shall not be construed as conferring any extension of statutory time for holding of AGMs (Annual General Meetings) by the companies under the Act and the companies which have not adhered to the relevant statutory timelines shall be liable under the relevant provisions of the Act".Under the Companies Act, entities must submit statutory filings through the MCA 21 portal. Recently, stakeholders have faced issues using the portal.The Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) said on Sunday that the extended timelines provide critical breathing room to navigate the technical transition to the MCA 21 V3 portal.The timely relief reflects the ministry's stakeholder-centric approach and commitment to ease of doing business, it said in a statement.The ministry implements the Companies Act.

items.title: Beyond heartbreak: How anger, fear and shock can temporarily stun the heart
items.summary:
Intense grief is not the only emotion that can affect the heart -- extreme anger, fear or shock can temporarily weaken the heart's pumping ability, triggering a rare condition known as Takotsubo cardiomyopathy or "broken heart syndrome", experts said.
Usually associated with a sudden surge of stress hormones following an intense emotional or physical event, the condition can be triggered by bereavement, relationship breakdown or extreme anger, highlighting the complex link between emotional stress and cardiovascular health.
"A sudden and intense emotional episode, including extreme anger, can trigger a powerful adrenaline response and temporarily affect the heart muscle's ability to contract normally. The trigger need not always be sadness or grief," said Dr Rajiv Narang, Head of the Department of Cardiology at AIIMS, Delhi.

As the rivalry intensifies, experts say the window for countries to be able to choose freely between the two AI superpowers may be narrowing, forcing them to at one point pick between the US-led Pax Silica and the China-inspired World AI Cooperation Organisation.
That could put many countries in a dilemma: Do they go with the US' most advanced chips and AI technologies, or join China's more affordable, open-source AI systems?
Kazakhstan, a Central Asia nation of about 21 million people, is a rare example of a country that has sought to bridge that gap.
Just three weeks after its AI minister Zhaslan Madiyev visited Washington in June to join the US group working to strengthen AI supply chains, he headed to Shanghai for a signing ceremony making the Central Asian country a founding member of China's .

A Central Railway (CR) spokesperson said a woman's bag caught fire following a suspected power bank explosion before the train reached Ghatkopar station. Thick smoke filled the compartment, prompting passengers to pull the alarm chain.

While nobody was injured, the female commuter's belongings were destroyed, the official said.
The train was halted at Ghatkopar station between 12.51 pm and 12.53 pm for safety checks. Railway staff inspected the train before it resumed its journey, the official added.

items.title: What's got Europe angry? Protests sweep nations
items.summary: Protests over the cost of living, strained public services and political accountability swept across France, Italy, Belgium and Albania on Saturday, with demonstrators clashing with police in several cities and authorities deploying tear gas, water cannons and large numbers of officers to contain unrest.The demonstrations reflected different domestic grievances but a common pattern of mounting public frustration, particularly over education, economic hardship and trust in political leadership. France saw the largest mobilisation, with more than 400,000 people taking to the streets nationwide, according to the Interior Ministry, while Albania witnessed a fresh escalation of anti-government protests after days of violence in its capital, Tirana.Also read: More than 400,000 protest across France, challenging Macron as Paris clashes eruptItaly saw renewed demonstrations against war and rising living costs, with clashes in Turin, Rome and Bologna, while hundreds of mainly young protesters gathered in Brussels to demand better conditions in education and challenge police conduct.The latest unrest follows a week of violence in France and Belgium, as authorities across the four countries grapple with demonstrations that have increasingly tested public order and political leadership.France: School funding and living costs fuel mass mobilisationMore than 400,000 people rallied across France on Saturday against school funding shortages and soaring living costs, posing a fresh challenge to President Emmanuel Macron's government in the final months of his presidency.The Interior Ministry estimated nationwide participation at 410,000, including 110,000 in Paris, while the CGT trade union put the figure at nearly 800,000. The Paris march began peacefully but ended in clashes near Porte de Vincennes, where some protesters threw projectiles and police deployed tear gas and water cannons.The Paris prosecutor's office said 64 people had been arrested in connection with the demonstration, including six minors, and 40 had been placed in police custody. The government had deployed up to 70,000 officers nationwide, supported by helicopters, armoured vehicles and water cannons.What began last month as a protest over staff shortages at a high school southeast of Paris has grown into a broader movement involving students and workers seeking better education, higher wages and improved pensions.Public middle and high schools lost 15.4 million teaching hours in the 2024-25 school year because absent teachers were not replaced, amounting to 7.5% of scheduled teaching time, according to Education Ministry figures.Students are demanding 250,000 additional higher-education places, more teachers, school repairs and increased student grants. They are also seeking a freeze on rents in public student housing.Economic pressures have added to the anger. French energy prices rose 21.3% in September from a year earlier, helping push overall inflation to 3.1%, according to national statistics agency INSEE.The unrest has become a test of Macron's authority, with the far-right National Rally accusing his government of failing to protect the public. Authorities banned demonstrations in several cities, including Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, drawing criticism from trade unions over freedom of expression.Also read: Italy sees fresh protests over war, cost of living as Police brace for violenceItaly: Anti-war rallies return as police brace for violenceItalian cities saw fresh protests against war and rising living costs on Saturday, a week after demonstrations escalated into clashes, looting and property damage.Turin, Rome and Bologna witnessed confrontations between police and demonstrators, while protests in Milan were largely peaceful, Reuters reported. Police maintained a heavy presence and many shops shut as a precaution against potential damage.Authorities strengthened security after calls for further demonstrations circulated on social media, seeking to prevent a repeat of the previous weekend's violence. Reuters witnesses did not observe shops being looted or property vandalised during Saturday's demonstrations.Earlier in the day, Italian police said they had detained a person allegedly linked to organising the 'October 17 Movement', associated with last weekend's protests, and taken the individual to police headquarters in Milan for questioning.The demonstrations brought together grievances over international conflict and the rising cost of living, although the reports did not establish a single nationwide political demand driving the rallies.Belgium: Young protesters clash with police over educationIn Brussels, hundreds of mainly young demonstrators gathered on Saturday to demand better conditions in education, continuing a series of rallies held over recent months.Police used tear gas and pepper spray as clashes broke out, with protesters accusing authorities of excessive violence and calling for greater education funding, Reuters witnesses and Belgian media reported.In one incident witnessed by Reuters, police pursued demonstrators who ran and fell to the ground, while officers hit and kicked one protester. Elsewhere, demonstrators threw road signs and other objects onto a pile of rental scooters and bicycles and attempted to set it alight.Belgian media also reported that police used tear gas to disperse a group of protesters.The clashes were smaller and less violent than those seen in Belgium the previous week and in neighbouring France, Reuters reported.Brussels police said no major incidents had occurred by the end of the afternoon. Officers temporarily detained five people for disturbing public order and four others over alleged possession of prohibited weapons and incitement to rioting.Albania: Anti-government anger widens beyond original grievancesThousands gathered in Tirana on Saturday for a fresh anti-government demonstration, as unrest that has shaken the Albanian capital since mid-October escalated again after several quieter days.Police fired tear gas, used water cannons and rubber bullets after some demonstrators threw stones at the education ministry, a focal point of the protests. Several government buildings have been attacked during the unrest, and authorities say more than 300 protesters and police officers have been injured. Dozens of demonstrators have also been detained.The movement has expanded beyond its original grievances into a broader campaign against corruption, poor public services and Prime Minister Edi Rama's government.Anti-government protests began in May over a luxury hotel project linked to US President Donald Trump's family. Scientists said in July that the development had already caused irreparable damage to a previously pristine stretch of Albania's coastline. Anger over the project subsequently broadened into demands for Rama to step down.Students have raised concerns about deteriorating education standards and limited opportunities, while economic hardship and emigration have added to public frustration. More than 1.5 million people have left Albania since the fall of Communism in the 1990s, leaving a population of about 2.3 million.

items.title: More than 400,000 protest across France
items.summary: Paris: Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to a close Saturday, with more than 400,000 people rallying across France over school funding and soaring living costs in a fresh challenge to President Emmanuel Macron's government.The Paris march began peacefully, a week after widespread rioting and looting during protests across the country. Near its endpoint at Porte de Vincennes, some protesters threw projectiles while police fired volleys of tear gas and used water cannons to disperse people.The Interior Ministry put nationwide turnout at 410,000, while the CGT union estimated nearly 800,000. The ministry's estimate included 110,000 in Paris, where authorities had confined the march to the city's southeastern edge, away from the center.Read more: Thousands march in France over schools and living costs as police use tear gasElsewhere in France, police used tear gas in Lyon, Clermont-Ferrand and Strasbourg and water cannons in Nice and Nantes, French media reported. In Marseille, officers fired tear gas during clashes with several dozen people near the march's endpoint.The Paris prosecutor's office said 64 people had been arrested in connection with Saturday's demonstration and 40 placed in police custody. Those arrested included six minors. Most arrests concerned suspected weapons offenses or participation in a group preparing violence or property damage, the office said.The unrest is testing Macron's authority in the final months of his presidency before voters choose his successor in May. The stakes are high: the far-right National Rally has accused his government of failing to protect the public and urged people to channel their anger into votes for them.Read more: ‘France’s protests increased polarisation — and helped the far-right’Interior Minister Laurent Nunez had announced a nationwide deployment of up to 70,000 officers, backed by helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons.Trade unions led the procession, followed by protesters in raincoats carrying flags and handmade placards.Camille Chesnier, 27, said she had been unable to find work despite having an engineering degree and a master's degree."There are enormous numbers of people in the same situation as me but who aren't privileged and who find themselves living on the streets and in squats and, frankly, it's very tough," she said.A small protest became a national movementWhat began last month as a protest over staff shortages at one high school southeast of Paris has spread nationwide, drawing students demanding better schools and workers seeking higher wages and pensions.In Paris, Benedicte Pittion, a 46-year-old teacher, marched through steady rain with her 16-year-old daughter, Garance, a high school student. Both had supported the movement from the start, but this was their first protest together."The young people who have been demonstrating have not been heard, and as a parent and as a teacher, I stand with them," Pittion said.Garance said she had been "really scared" to attend after seeing images of last weekend's violence, but argued that staying away would hand the government a victory.Public middle and high schools lost 15.4 million teaching hours in the 2024-25 school year because absent teachers were not replaced, according to Education Ministry figures. That amounted to 7.5% of scheduled teaching time.Macron met high school representatives Friday. They said he had promised to overhaul university admissions, but called for protests to continue until concrete measures are announced.Organizers from the "yellow vest" protest movement called for another day of rallies Oct. 31 to defend the right to demonstrate.Some protests were bannedSoumaya Abed, a 58-year-old nurse wearing a red CGT union vest, said she had been joining protests for more than 30 years, but had never seen one start at Porte d'Italie, on the capital's outskirts."They are using what happened last week as an excuse to quiet protesters," she said. "But it won't stop the movement. It won't stop students from demanding better conditions in schools."In Marseille, police put attendance at 17,000, while the CGT union estimated 100,000. In the southwestern city of Toulouse, 26,500 people joined the protests, according to authorities. Authorities had banned rallies in cities including Lyon, Nice and Montpellier.Trade unions have criticized the bans, calling them violations of freedom of expression, which is protected by the constitution.Thousands also marched Saturday in Orleans, south of Paris, in a separate peaceful protest against the far right as Marine Le Pen's National Rally held a two-day congress in the city.Macron, a centrist, has entered the crisis in the final stretches of his term with his popularity at its lowest since he took office in 2017. He has said that the measures are needed to protect city centers, businesses and public buildings.Nunez acknowledged Monday that police had lost control in some cities during last weekend's unrest, when more than half a million people took to the streets and some 3,000 shops across France were damaged or looted amid street violence not seen in years.He offered to resign, but Macron refused the offer.Shops board up and museums closeGendarmes stood guard Saturday beneath the Arc de Triomphe and shopkeepers boarded up storefronts across Paris. Near the Saint-Lazare train station Saturday, Akram Ahmed, a 34-year-old contractor, was boarding up an optician's shop."I got the call last night," he said. "The owner seemed desperate. He said I was saving his life."Major museums, including the Louvre, Orsay Museum, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais - where a major Cezanne exhibit is on display - were shuttered Saturday.Art Basel, one of the world's most prestigious contemporary art fairs, opened to the public Friday, but only for the day, with the threat of unrest prompting organizers to cancel the weekend program.Students and workers are angryStudent groups want 250,000 more places in higher education and an end to selection through Parcoursup, the national admissions system.Their joint 10-point plan also calls for more teachers and repairs to schools and universities.They are also seeking help with everyday costs: an extra 200 euros ($224) a month in student grants and a rent freeze in public student housing.Energy prices in France were 21.3% higher in September than a year earlier, helping drive overall inflation to 3.1%, according to the national statistics agency, INSEE.Paris protester Louis Ledoux--Xatard voiced frustration over inequality."Looking at countries like the United States, we don't want to end up like them, where part of the population has everything and the others have nothing," he said."I never imagined that I'd be taking to the streets so much before my thirties."

items.summary: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal announced that the Indian government is working to pinpoint occupations least susceptible to artificial intelligence (AI). The strategy targets sectors where AI can boost efficiency rather than displace human labor, allowing India to capitalize on its skilled labor force and heritage strengths.Speaking to Indian science and technology students and researchers in Germany, Goyal explained that he instructed his ministry to map out future-proof roles to help guide the nation's employment roadmap.“I got my ministry to start working on what are the AI proof professions..After all we have to plan as a nation for so many millions of people. What are the sectors where the AI can at max add to efficiency, not necessary replace (human workforce),” he said.He highlighted that India is well-positioned to lead globally in domains dependent on human creativity and heritage, including handlooms, handicrafts, tourism, and culinary arts.“Also, given the traditional skills that many of us in India acquire. So, our handicraft, handloom no amount of AI can replace that,” he said.Goyal emphasized that prioritizing areas with distinct competitive advantages will directly benefit the nation's population.“There are many, many areas where I think we have some very special strengths which we will be focusing on also simultaneously developing to ensure that 1.4 billion people have a better life in the future,” Goyal said.When questioned about potential state support or incentives for these industries, Goyal noted that assistance would stem from various channels based on specific needs.“It will be a mix of several initiatives, some privately led, some government led, some people led, some opportunity led,” he said.Additionally, the minister outlined efforts to attract Indian scientists, engineers, and researchers currently based overseas back to India. He invited input from the Indian academic community in Germany regarding the ideal conditions for returning.“I have asked them (researchers and students) to tell us what they will need in order to consider and how can we support more, young researchers or our talented engineers and scientific community to come and work and serve in India,” he said.Goyal observed that bringing talent back home requires more than just monetary offers; it depends on building a robust ecosystem for innovation.“And surprisingly, I realize it’s not just about money, it’s about the enabling environment, the support of the ecosystem,” he said.To facilitate this, Goyal plans to consult with private and public academic bodies, research institutes, and industry leaders to foster collaborative opportunities. His comments align with broader efforts to fortify India's innovation framework as automation reshapes global employment trends.Remarking on the sentiment among Indian students in Germany, Goyal pointed out a growing desire to return and join India's expanding economy.“This large Indian student community, full of enthusiasm, seems to be very excited about taking their learnings back to India. Now we can see them not just looking for a job in Germany, but wanting to be back home to contribute to the India growth story, because that is where the action is,” he told reporters.Data from the report indicates that Germany is home to approximately 330,000 people of Indian origin alongside 60,000 to 70,000 Indian students. Goyal visited Germany to meet with commercial and political figures to expand trade and investment channels between the two countries.

items.title: UK tells Britons to stockpile essentials
items.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged Britons to be better prepared for emergencies saying that unexpected events are becoming increasingly common. The remarks came as the government rolled out its new ‘Be Ready’ initiative, which asks households to keep essential supplies at home for three days.“We're having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we're living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common,” Burnham said on Friday.Also Read: Immigration to UK from third-world countries, including Pakistan, will end entirely, British MP Rupert Lowe warnsWhy is the UK asking people to prepare for emergencies?The advisory comes amid concerns about disruptions caused by severe weather, cyberattacks and other unexpected events.The UK has experienced storms, droughts, extreme heat and wildfires in recent years. These events can damage infrastructure and disrupt essential services. They can also affect access to electricity, water, phone networks and the internet.Also Read: Don't panic: UK govt tells Britons to 'be ready' for emergenciesCybersecurity incidents have added to these concerns. Recent cyberattacks affecting French supermarket chains disrupted refrigeration systems. Stores were forced to discard spoiled food. Separately, a software security incident involving PHP, a programming language used by many websites, prompted organisations to shut down websites.The campaign also reflects a wider European push for emergency preparedness. France, Ireland and the Netherlands have issued similar guidance. These recommendations encourage households to prepare to manage disruptions for three days.What does the emergency checklist include?The official ‘Be Ready’ checklist recommends keeping enough essential supplies at home to manage for three days. It covers eight broad categories.Water- Bottled water for three days.- At least three litres per person per day for drinking.- Additional water for cooking and washing.2. Food- Three days' worth of non-perishable food.- Long-lasting food that does not need refrigeration or cooking.- Examples include tinned meat, fish and vegetables, dried fruit and nuts.- The government recommends choosing food that household members would normally eat.3. Hygiene- Hand sanitiser.- Wet wipes.- Essential hygiene and bathroom products.4. Light and warmth- A torch and spare batteries.- Blankets and sleeping bags.- Warm clothing to help households cope if heating is disrupted.5. Communication and information- A battery-powered or wind-up FM radio to receive updates during outages.- A charged power bank to keep phones running.6. Money and documents- Cash in a mix of coins and banknotes.- Payment cards in case electronic payment systems or ATMs stop working.- Copies of important documents, including identification.- A written list of important phone numbers.- Information about regular medication and dosages.7. Medical and health supplies- A first-aid kit with basic supplies.- Essential medicines and other medical supplies.8. Baby and pet supplies- Baby formula, nappies and wipes for households with infants.- Ready-to-feed formula is recommended. Preparing powdered formula safely may be difficult if water cannot be boiled.- Pet food and bottled water for animals.The government has advised people not to buy everything at once. Households should first check what they already have. They can then identify missing items and add them during regular shopping trips. This approach also helps spread the cost.The checklist recommends reviewing supplies every six months. People should check expiry dates and replace items when necessary. They should also update their kits as household needs change.The government also encouraged people to speak to their neighbours. They can exchange contact details and discuss how to help one another during an outage. Those with extra supplies may consider donating them to people who cannot afford to prepare their own households.The government has separately encouraged eligible households to sign up to the Priority Services Register. The register helps electricity, gas and water providers identify customers who may need additional assistance during service interruptions.

items.title: Explained: What are rolling returns in mutual funds and how do you calculate them?
items.summary: Rolling returns measure a mutual fund scheme’s annualised returns over a specified period, calculated at regular intervals such as daily, monthly or yearly. By averaging returns across multiple overlapping periods, they provide a more comprehensive view of a fund’s performance and consistency over time. Compared with trailing returns, which reflect performance up to a single point in time, rolling returns can offer a more balanced assessment of how a fund has performed across different market conditions.Trailing returns have a recency bias and point-to-point returns are specific to the period taken for analysis. On the other hand, rolling return measures the fund's absolute and relative performance across all time periods without any bias.Also Read |Parag Parikh ELSS Tax Saver Fund underperforms benchmark for 3 years despite 5-star rating. Should investors worry?Rolling returns gives a comprehensive picture of the performance by a fund. Due to different time periods involved, the return consistency of the fund over a defined time period can be analysed efficiently as it considers both upstream and downstream in the market.Looking to calculate rolling returns for your mutual fund investments in excel? Here is how you can calculate:Suppose you are investing in an ABC fund for a time period of five years as this time frame is the minimum horizon an equity investor should have.  Step 1: Assuming an investor wants to test the five year returns of an ABC scheme over 15 long years. Start with the daily NAV of the scheme. items.title: Typhoon Champi kills one, injures 350 in Taiwan; 280,000 homes lose power
items.summary:
Typhoon Champi killed one person and injured hundreds in Taiwan, as well as downing trees and knocking out power for hundreds of thousands of people as the storm's strong winds and rains continued overnight Friday into Saturday morning.
Although Champi did not hit Taiwan directly, the storm's span was large enough to impact most of Taiwan. The island's weather authorities said the storm was weakening Saturday morning and that by evening, the land warnings for the typhoon would be removed.
Taiwan's Central Emergency Operations Centre reported that 350 were injured as of Friday night. The one death was a man who was washed away by waves in Taiwan's Pingtung county, the island's southernmost part.
The storm knocked out power for 280,000 households, according to United Daily News, a local Taiwanese newspaper, citing the island's power authorities. But power had returned to 80 per cent of households by Saturday morning.
Across the island, the storm downed trees and signs, some smaller .

items.title: Infosys CEO: Macro recovery ‘more uneven’
items.summary: Infosys had expected technology spending to recover in the second half of FY27, but the improvement is proving more uneven than anticipated, chief executive Salil Parekh said, as the IT services company cut its revenue growth guidance for the year.“We had a sense that the macro was settling down, so we had a guidance where the upper end looked at maybe things would settle down in the second half. Things are a little bit more uneven,” Parekh said during the post-results press conference.He added that technology spending could still stabilise over time, allowing the company to benefit if client budgets recover.Also Read: Infosys ADRs crash 6% after Q2 results as revenue guidance cut spooks investorsThe comments came as Infosys cut its FY27 revenue growth guidance in constant currency terms to 1-2% from 1.5-3% earlier, reflecting a more cautious view of the pace of recovery.Parekh said the revised guidance reflected what the company was seeing in the market rather than a precise prediction of when spending would improve.AI gains traction, but broad-based recovery remains elusiveWhile AI-related work is growing, the company is also seeing productivity gains from AI affect parts of its traditional services business as clients seek to lower costs.Parekh said the company had not quantified this compression but remained focused on growing AI-led revenue to offset the impact over time.Chief financial officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said AI-related revenue had risen to 8.2% of total revenue from 5.5% in the third quarter, with double-digit sequential growth over recent quarters.Parekh said the company saw a substantial long-term opportunity in AI services, with an addressable market of about $300 billion across six focus areas.However, the recovery remains uneven across industries. Parekh said Infosys was yet to see a pickup in retail, while communications remained another challenging segment.North America had also been softer over recent quarters, partly due to lower discretionary spending and client-specific ramp-downs, Sanghrajka said.Also Read: Infosys Q2 Results: Profit rises 6% YoY to Rs 7,823 crore; co lowers revenue guidanceThe company reported large deal wins worth $3.6 billion in the quarter, of which 61% was net new business. Sanghrajka said a major net-new deal would contribute minimally to FY27 revenue as it was expected to ramp up only towards the end of the fourth quarter, but could add more than 1% to revenue growth next year.Infosys retained its FY27 operating margin guidance of 20-22%.

items.title: India business sentiment rebounds in Q2 FY27: NCAER
items.summary: India’s business sentiment rebounded in the second quarter of this fiscal year, with the Business Confidence Index (BCI) rising to 107.8 from 99.8 in the April–June quarter, ending a four-quarter period of moderation driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions, according to the latest NCAER Business Expectations Survey.Conducted in September by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), the survey sampled 502 companies across different sizes in six major cities: Delhi NCR in the north, Bengaluru and Chennai in the south, Kolkata in the east, and Mumbai and Pune in the west."Though BCI improved, it was lower than the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year (142.6 in 2025−26: Q2)," it said.Also read: India October business growth hits 4-month high; hiring stalls, PMI showsThe BCI evaluates four key parameters: expectations of improved macro-economic conditions over the next six months, expectations of better firm financial health over the next six months, a favorable current investment climate, and present capacity utilization at or near optimal levels.All four parameters recorded gains, driving the quarter-over-quarter uptick in business sentiment."The share of firms expecting 'overall economic conditions to improve in the next six months' increased from 43 per cent in 2026-27: Q1 to 50 per cent in 2026-27: Q2," NCAER said.Confidence regarding firm financial prospects over the coming six months expanded from 37% in Q1 to 41% in Q2. Similarly, positive assessments of the current investment climate grew from 26% to 30%. Opinions on optimal capacity utilization also saw an increase, climbing from 91% in the first quarter to 94% in the second.Segment-wise, the BCI for MSMEs moved up from 93 to 100, while for large enterprises it rose from 111.6 to 120.3.NCAER's Bornali Bhandari, who led the survey, said, "The data indicate a broad-based recovery in sentiments across both MSMEs and large firms"."Overall business prospects improved both domestically and externally, and cost sentiments have moderated," she added.

items.title: Himadri Speciality Chemicals plans ₹1,613-cr capacity expansion
items.summary:
Himadri Speciality Chemicals Ltd has drawn up a growth roadmap centred on capacity expansion, margin improvement and profit acceleration, as it aims at building the materials backbone for the energy transition economy, a top company official said.
The company plans to invest Rs 1,125 crore in lithium iron phosphate (LFP), Rs 248 crore in speciality chemicals, Rs 70 crore in carbon nanotubes and Rs 170 crore in super speciality carbon black, according to its investor presentation for the July-September quarter.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas issued operational guidelines for the Samudra Manthan programme, which aims to improve the economics of exploring India's deepwater and ultra-deepwater basins, where high drilling costs and uncertain geological prospects have constrained investment.

Sardar Patel Vidyalaya in Lodi Estate, Venkateshwar Global School in Rohini, and Salwan Public School in Mayur Vihar received the threat emails, following which authorities were informed.

State-owned Oil India Ltd. (OIL) on Friday said it has made a natural gas discovery in a shallow-water Krishna Godavari basin block that the firm had won in recent Discovered Small Field (DSF) bid rounds.
The discovery was made in the previously unappraised Matsyapuri formation in the Krishna-Godavari Basin off India's east coast, recording a peak test flow of 200,000 Standard Cubic Metres Per Day (SCMD), the state-run explorer said in a statement.

The well has flowed gas at about 100,000 SCMD, with a maximum rate of 200,000 SCMD recorded during continuous testing. The company also reported condensate output of about 170 barrels per day.

Sanjib Raha, alias Sentu, was initially detained from a hideout in Nadia district on Thursday and later arrested, a senior officer said.
"There were two persons who were making announcements at the Chorbagan Durga Puja. He was one of them. He had been absconding since the incident occurred in the evening of October 17. We initially detained him in Nadia and then arrested him after hours of questioning," he said.
At least 19 people died, and 25 others were injured in the stampede at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata following a crowd surge amid rain.

items.title: ITBP has raised drone platoons, building bunkers along LAC, says DG
items.summary:
The ITBP has raised drone platoons in all its border units, prepared a new 'Strike' course to better handle Galwan-like battles and is creating underground infrastructure along the front "in a big way" as part of the new warfare to counter India's "biggest adversary" China, the force's chief said on Thursday.
ITBP Director General (DG) Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor told his troops at a force base in Rajasthan's Alwar that countering China through "traditional" means of warfare was a thing of the past and hence they were investing in modernizing the force, its weapons, vehicles and border posts.
The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), raised in 1962, guards the 3,488-km-long Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China.
The DG noted that the recent Ukraine-Russia and Iran-US wars have shown the importance of drone and anti-drone technology through which a small country can overwhelm a bigger nation during conflict.

items.title: No dilution in standards: NMC on denotification of medical education rules
items.summary:
The National Medical Commission has asserted that the de-notification of the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 will not dilute prescribed standards of medical education and are intended to remove overlapping procedures.
The Commission, which is the statutory body for medical education in the country, had on October 14 denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations (MSMER-2023).
The denotification "does not, in any manner, dilute the prescribed standards of medical education or the regulatory oversight exercised by NMC," a statement by the Commission said.
Under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, the Undergraduate Medical Education Board (UGMEB) and Postgraduate Medical Education Board (PGMEB) are primarily entrusted with prescribing academic standards, minimum requirements and educational norms.
The Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB), under Section 26 of the Act is specifically empowered to assess and inspect .

items.title: Rupee rises 3 paise to 94.78 against US dollar during early trade
items.summary:
The rupee traded in a narrow range and edged up 3 paise to 94.78 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday amid elevated crude oil prices and foreign fund outflows.
Forex traders said rupee is under pressure amid persistent macroeconomic headwinds, including global dollar strength and Brent crude prices hovering near USD 113 per barrel.
At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.78, registering a gain of 3 paise over its previous close.
On Thursday, the rupee closed at 94.81 against the American currency.
Foreign investors turned cautious seeking safe-haven greenback assets amid elevated US Treasury yields,  said Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP.
Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 101.64, higher by 0.04 per cent.

items.title: Asian Para Games: Sandeep, Haney clinch gold with world records for India
items.summary:
India's Sandeep and Haney won gold medals with world record performances in the men's 400m T64 and men's javelin throw F37/38 events respectively at the Asian Para Games here on Friday.
Sandeep clocked 52.28 seconds, a world record, to win the 400m T64 final at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium. He finished 0.85 seconds ahead of Saudi Arabia's Nour Alsana (53.13, season's best). Indian compatriot Ajay Kumar took bronze in 53.61, a Games Record, while China's Huang Ruihua was fourth with a personal best of 54.39.
In the javelin throw F37/38 final at the same venue, Haney produced a world record throw of 60.49m for gold, scoring 1116 Raza points. Iran's Hormoz Seidikazpounji took silver with a personal best of 50.68m (1009 points), while China's Yu Chengjie claimed bronze with an Asian record 53.66m (943 points).
India have thus reached 100 medals in total in this edition of the sporting extravaganza.

items.summary: FIFA opened the bidding process for US media rights to the 2030 World Cup on Thursday along with an option to secure the 2034 edition, adding that it has yet to decide whether to keep the controversial hydration breaks introduced this year that opened up additional advertising windows ​for broadcasters.FIFA said in a press release that it was open to "innovative approaches" to reach large audiences and that the bid submission deadline is November 19.Fox held the exclusive English-language FIFA broadcast rights in the United States for the last three World Cups, including the 2026 edition that was co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico, while Telemundo held the Spanish language rights during that same time.Spain, which won the 2026 World Cup, will co-host the 2030 edition with Portugal and ‌Morocco, ⁠although Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay will also stage matches to mark the tournament's 100th anniversary. Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cup.FIFA Chief Business Officer Romy Gai, speaking to reporters after the announcement, said world soccer's governing body is still evaluating whether to keep the hydration breaks that were put in place for the 2026 World Cup to help players cope with high temperatures but also proved lucrative for broadcasters.The hydration breaks fuelled debate over their impact on the game, with some viewers complaining ​about being exposed to commercials during the three-minute stoppages in each half."If the average temperature will be higher than the normal average is in these countries we expect to confirm having the hydration break, but not automatically," said Gai."It's not the final decision because this is something that we need to further engage with all the stakeholders."According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup averaged 13.5 million viewers per match on linear and streaming platforms in the United States, up 166% on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.Earlier this week, Netflix announced that it secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup ​in Spain and Andorra.The Saudi climate will likely force FIFA to hold the 2034 tournament in the Northern Hemisphere winter, just like it did for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, but Gai said that while it is a possibility the matter has not yet been discussed officially."It's too early for that. But this is something that we are concretely considering," Gai said when asked about staging the 2034 World Cup in November-December of that year instead of the tournament's traditional June-July slot."It will be further assessed and we will share the same comments with any bidders when it will be the time to sit down and analyze how it can be to play the World Cup in 2034. It is a clear possibility ... but it's not yet confirmed. So we need to understand more."

items.summary: French police have taken 2,700 people into custody since Saturday in connection with riots and looting, Reuters reported citing Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin, as authorities brace for further unrest across the country."Some 2,700 people have been taken into police custody since Saturday in connection with these riots and looting," Darmanin said in an interview with French news channel LCI.French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be prohibited in the coming days. He blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting.Speaking after a meeting with intelligence chiefs and senior ministers, Macron said demonstrations organised by groups such as trade unions would be permitted, although authorities could divert them to alternative routes to protect businesses."Last Saturday we had political and seditious acts by ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic," he said.His remarks came as authorities across France prepared for fresh protests following some of the country's worst urban unrest in years.Darmanin said he wanted voting rights to be suspended for people who violate bans on demonstrations. He also called for restrictions on social media access for those involved in violence, looting or attacks on police.Authorities have banned all protests scheduled for Saturday in Marseille and Lyon, France's second- and third-largest cities. However, new demonstrations are already being planned ahead of a weekend that officials fear could turn volatile.France's main student union, UNEF, has called for rallies on Saturday, while the Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that emerged in 2018, has submitted plans for a march through central Paris.Businesses in central Paris have started boarding up their shop windows in anticipation of possible violence. Luxury goods group Hermes said it had strengthened security at its stores across France.Organisers of Art Basel Paris, an international art collectors fair being held in an exhibition hall in central Paris, said the event would remain closed throughout the weekend.In the northern city of Orleans, authorities were preparing for possible unrest as the far-right National Rally prepared to hold its annual meeting, while unions and left-wing groups planned demonstrations.A student protest scheduled for Thursday in Paris was initially banned but was later permitted to proceed. However, transit authorities shut metro stations in central Paris in anticipation of unauthorised gatherings.PUBLIC ANGERFrance was shaken by violence on the fringes of nationwide protests on October 17, exposing the extent of public anger and raising concerns about the ability of security services to maintain order.Two people have been arrested in connection with an arson attack on the city hall in Limoges, according to French officials and media reports.A third consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas affected by the violence, giving the government some respite ahead of the weekend.The unrest has also exposed deeper discontent in France, where rising energy costs, mounting pressure on household budgets and concerns about deteriorating public services have fuelled frustration among workers and younger people.France's political class has meanwhile become embroiled in a bitter blame game, with the government accusing far-left political groups of fuelling the unrest.(With inputs from Reuters)

items.title: 7.0 earthquake in Tibet kills at least 16
items.summary: Beijing: A strong earthquake killed at least 16 people and injured 46 in China's remote Tibet region, state media said, citing local authorities.More than 300 houses collapsed in the 7.0 magnitude quake, which struck on Thursday at 10:33 pm (1433 GMT).Officials were still evaluating the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, state news agency Xinhua said.China Central Television (CCTV) put the number of injured at 46, 11 of them seriously, with 339 houses collapsed or damaged, citing local officials.Videos posted by CCTV showed workers running out of restaurants and objects falling off shelves at supermarkets when the quake struck.The epicentre was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres (120 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.It struck at a shallow depth of around 10 kilometres.A level-III earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, CCTV reported.The epicentre was in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in the walls, according to Xinhua.Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.More than 300 police officers have been dispatched for relief work while the regional fire and rescue corps has mobilised 347 personnel to the affected areas, Xinhua reported.Rescue workers clambered through damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs, and carrying one person, footage on CCTV showed.It also showed rescue workers shining flashlights on other damaged buildings and soldiers lining up ready to be deployed.Earthquakes in China are relatively common.In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in an earthquake in Tibet's rural Tingri county.In December 2023, a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China killed at least 127 people, according to state media.That quake was China's deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people died in the southwestern province of Yunnan.A huge tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left some 90,000 people dead or missing, including around 5,000 schoolchildren.

items.title: ITBP DG gives a peek into troops' LAC plan
items.summary: New Delhi: The ITBP has raised drone platoons in all its border units, prepared a new 'Strike' course to better handle Galwan-like battles and is creating underground infrastructure along the front "in a big way" as part of the new warfare to counter India's "biggest adversary" China, the force's chief said on Thursday.ITBP Director General (DG) Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor told his troops at a force base in Rajasthan's Alwar that countering China through "traditional" means of warfare was a thing of the past and hence they were investing in modernizing the force, its weapons, vehicles and border posts.The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), raised in 1962, guards the 3,488-km-long Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China.The DG noted that the recent Ukraine-Russia and Iran-US wars have shown the importance of drone and anti-drone technology through which a small country can overwhelm a bigger nation during conflict.Also read | Army invites applications for 75-day internship programme in defence technologiesKapoor, who is set to retire from service on October 31, addressed his troops during an investiture ceremony held leading up to the force's 65th Raising Day on October 24.He said the China front was our "most difficult" border, and China was a "powerful" neighbour and India's "biggest adversary," requiring enhanced capabilities to "counter" it."Drones have become a major challenge and an opportunity also. It will be difficult to compete with China using traditional methods... They have modernised and invested heavily in their PLA but drones are such that a small country can give a befitting contest to a bigger nation," he said.He noted that almost 10,000-15,000 Russian troops are killed in the war with Ukraine every month."This is despite the fact that it (Russia) is a big country and a superpower. They (Russia) thought that they would capture (Ukraine) in 1-2 months but it is the fourth year counting, and every month they (Russians) have 10-15 thousand bodies reaching them," the DG said.He added that this caused such "big damage" and that Russia was suffering because of that one decision.Kapoor then cited the Iran-US war as an example, noting that Iran, without an Air Force, Navy, or Army, engaged in combat with the global superpower.Also read | From 290-km BrahMos to a proposed 1,500-km variant: How Operation Sindoor boosted India's missile profile"The role of traditional armies has changed since the drones arrived, and we must embrace drone and anti-drone systems in a big way," he said.Kapoor said the approximately 95,000-personnel-strong, mountain-warfare-trained ITBP has received government funds worth Rs 400 crore and 70 per cent of these funds have been earmarked for enhancing the force's drone warfare capabilities."Each border guarding battalion now has a drone platoon, and we are training drone pilots and building drones too.""The Ministry of Home Affairs has also granted in-principle approval to a bigger modernisation scheme of Rs 4,000 crore, of which we will earmark Rs 1,000 crore for drone and anti-drone systems," the DG said.He informed the troops that a new course named 'Strike' has been developed to train ITBP personnel, which will enhance their capabilities to face Galwan-like situations. The entire force will undergo this training by the end of 2027.Chinese soldiers used stones, nail-studded sticks, iron rods and clubs while carrying out brutal attacks on Indian soldiers along the LAC at Galwan (Ladakh) in June, 2020 resulting in 20 casualties on the Indian side while China belatedly claimed only 4 of its troops were killed. Multiple reports suggested that the Chinese fatalities were much higher.The ITBP chief added that a new combat team, the Shaurya commandos, has been raised. This team displayed its skills during the "ongoing" faceoff with the Chinese PLA troops at multiple places in Arunachal Pradesh.These commandos will be in every border battalion and will give the force a distinct identity, he said.The DG said the force was constructing underground shelters (bunkers) at border locations "in a big way," learning from the lessons of the new warfare, as above-ground buildings can become a target in 'hot war' situations, indicating the post-Operation Sindoor conflict with Pakistan.He said a pilot project is underway in this context and they plan to have these under-ground shelters in the coming years, equipped with the same comfort available in above-ground buildings.Kapoor said the force also worked on the ensuring the comfort and operational prepardeness of the troops by insulating 342 out of 383 barracks present in areas which face "sub-zero" temperatures, has procured 141 generator sets to ensure electricity at remote troop locations and got solar water heaters installed at a number of such facilities."This will help enhance the morale and confidence of the troops and improve the ITBP's operational preparedness," he said.The DG added that a 'cold start kit' was provided to border units which helps vehicles get immediate ignition in icy weather."Many years ago when we were in Kosovo in sub zero temperatures the vehicles there used to start in one crank. We wondered why this wasn't happening here? We did some experiments and now we can do it," he said.The DG also asked his troops to keep fit and healthy, saying a new diet plan has been introduced in the force and the "very high" content of sugar and oil has been lessened.He expressed concern over the cases of Alcohol Dependence Syndrome (ADS) in the ITBP which have doubled or tripled since 2020.The DG also asked the troops to be cautious against ADS and 'honey trap' instances of being lured by someone into sharing sensitive information through the social media.He added that the ITBP was also modernising its weapons, some of which are about 50 years old, and improving mobility through the procurement of new all-terrain Vehicles, ground vehicles and quick reaction vehicles,We have prepared a plan to become a specialised high-altitude mountain fighting force through all these measures, Kapoor said.

items.title: Wall Street dumps AI for Buffett’s Berkshire
items.summary: For three weeks, Wall Street sold one of the market’s hottest trades and bought one of its oldest. Chip stocks fell about 15 per cent. Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway rose about 7 per cent.Between October 2 and October 20, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) lost 15.1 per cent, while Berkshire’s Class B shares (BRK-B) gained 7.4 per cent, according to Yahoo Finance.On Tuesday, BRK-B closed at a record high for the first time since May 2, 2025, the day before Buffett said Greg Abel would take over as CEO.On Wednesday, both the Class B and Class A (BRK-A) shares touched new intraday records.Berkshire hits a record as chip stocks slump 15%: the rare dot-com-era signal investors are watching, and what it may mean for your portfolioThe wait was long. In those 17 months, the S&P 500 gained more than 35 per cent, and Berkshire only now got back to a record close.The recent moves have been strikingly one-sided. From October 6 to Tuesday, SOXX fell in 10 of 11 sessions, and Berkshire rose on nine of those days.On the chip sector’s two worst days, October 14 and October 16, Berkshire posted two of its best gains of the run. Since October 1, the stock has mostly gone up on days when chips went down.For now, that makes Berkshire look like a hedge against the AI chip trade.Berkshire is on track to rise in 14 of its last 15 sessions. It also strung together a 10-day winning streak, its first since 2018.The gap between the two is historic too. Over the 12 sessions from October 2 through Tuesday, Berkshire beat SOXX by 22 percentage points.Yahoo Finance compared Berkshire with the PHLX Semiconductor Index going back to 1994, and found this is the widest 12-session gap since early 2010. The all-time record, set in April 2000, was close to 40 points.The gap alone is not the rarest part. The combination is. Chips fell at least 14 per cent while Berkshire gained at least 7 per cent over 12 sessions. Before this month, that last happened on October 3, 2001. Every earlier case came in 1995-96 or in 2000-01, when the dot-com bubble was bursting.History gives a mixed message from here. In the short term, chips bounced back. They were higher a week later in five of the six earlier cases, and they are rebounding on Wednesday as well. A year later, the picture was weaker: chips were lower in five of six cases, and the S&P 500 fell in four.Under Abel, Berkshire is also using its cash differently. It bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the second quarter. That ended 14 straight quarters in which it sold more of its own stock than it bought, and its cash pile has come down from a record $397 billion.Buffett said on September 18 that he would step down as chairman too. The stock hit its low about two weeks later.The tech bets are changing as well. A few years ago, Apple made up nearly 45 per cent of Berkshire’s invested assets. Buffett was never known as a tech investor. What drew him to Apple was customer loyalty and people’s willingness to pay premium prices for iPhones, Macs and iPads, not the technology itself.In just a few months, Alphabet has become for Abel what Apple was for Buffett. Google handled roughly 90 per cent of global internet search traffic in September, which is part of the appeal. But the AI ambitions are what interest both men most. Since Alphabet added generative AI and large language models to Google Cloud, the world’s third-largest cloud platform, sales in that high-margin business have grown very fast.Abel is also looking beyond Alphabet. An October 14 filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission shows Berkshire is buying 10 million shares of Bending Spoons in a private placement at $33 a share, an investment of $330 million. It follows a $600 million investment at the company’s IPO in July.The company’s model has some similarity to Berkshire’s own. Berkshire grew to a $1 trillion market value by buying about five dozen companies, and pieces of others, and usually holding them for a long time.Bending Spoons, based in Italy, buys technology platforms and uses software, AI, price hikes and layoffs to make them leaner and to sell more subscriptions. So far it has bought AOL, Vimeo, Brightcove, Eventbrite and WeTransfer, among others. The company is already profitable and growing quickly.The next test comes with Berkshire’s third-quarter results, expected on Saturday, November 7.

items.title: Gold hits 2-month low as Silver prices slide
items.summary: Gold rate today fell to its lowest level since August 4. Spot gold slid 1.9 per cent to $4,060.37 per ounce to its lowest level in more than two months on Thursday. US gold futures for December delivery fell 1.8 per cent to $4,075.70 per ounce. This comes as a rally in oil prices heightened inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision next week.Spot silver dropped 3.9 per cent to $55.7225 per ounce, platinum slid 2.9 per cent to $1,581.73, its lowest since July 29, while palladium fell 2.5 per cent to $1,059.75 after hitting its lowest level since June 2025.Gold Rate Prediction"Gold prices can fall further... because we are still seeing a lot of uncertainty around the energy market," said Soni Kumari, analyst at ANZ.135100704Brent prices rose to their highest since May after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns over a broader escalation of conflict and further disruptions to crude oil supplies from the world's key exporting region.Meanwhile, US consumer and producer inflation data came in hotter than expected last week, largely on higher energy costs. That strengthens the case for tighter policy, even though Fed officials are still expected to hold off when they meet on October 27-28.While gold is typically considered a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates reduce the appeal of the non-yielding asset.Goldman Sachs expects one more 25-basis-point hike in December, lifting the peak policy rate range to 4.00 per cent-4.25 per cent. Traders are pricing in an 86 per cent likelihood of a December increase, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.135094387US Personal Consumption Expenditures data, set for release on October 29 and closely watched by the central bank, could give more clues on rate outlook."Given that the PCE data will show that prices rose at an uncomfortably high pace for the Fed, the FOMC communications may strike a hawkish tone and that could weigh on gold prices," said Hamad Hussain, climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics.

items.title: US visitor visa wait hits 12 months in India
items.summary: Indian applicants seeking US business and tourist visas may have to wait up to 12 months for the next available interview appointment in Mumbai. Hyderabad follows with a 10.5-month wait, while New Delhi has an estimated wait of 11 months, according to the department’s Global Visa Wait Times update dated October 21.Kolkata applicants face an estimated 8.5-month wait for the next available appointment, while Chennai has a 7.5-month wait. Mumbai also records the highest average wait time among the five cities at 12.5 months, measured from visa fee payment to the interview date in the previous month.Also Read: Australia’s new arrival control law raises questions for students and workers returning homeThe waiting period varies considerably by visa category. Applicants seeking student and exchange visitor visas generally face shorter queues, while appointment availability for petition-based work visas differs across consular posts.City-wise US visa appointment wait timesIndian cityVisitor visa (B1/B2): Average waitNext available visitor visa slotStudent/exchange visa (F, M, J)Petition-based work visa (H, L, O, P, Q)Mumbai12.5 months12 months4 months2 monthsHyderabad10.5 months10.5 months1 month6.5 monthsNew Delhi7 months11 months3 months3.5 monthsKolkata8.5 months8.5 months2.5 months1 monthChennai7.5 months7.5 months3.5 months2.5 monthsSource: US Department of State, Global Visa Wait Times, updated October 21, 2026.Student visa slots available soonerThe data shows that applicants seeking F, M and J visas, which cover student and exchange visitor categories, generally face shorter waits than visitor visa applicants.Also Read: Norway named best among National Geographic's world travel map for 2027; Indian city among the topHyderabad has the shortest estimated wait in this category at one month, followed by Kolkata at 2.5 months. New Delhi applicants face a three-month wait, while Chennai and Mumbai have estimated waits of 3.5 months and four months, respectively.For petition-based visas, including H, L, O, P and Q categories, Kolkata has the shortest estimated wait at one month. Mumbai follows at two months, while Chennai and New Delhi have waits of 2.5 months and 3.5 months, respectively. Hyderabad has the longest wait in this category at 6.5 months.The figures cover grouped visa categories and should not be interpreted as separate estimates for individual classifications such as H-1B or L-1 visas.Although, the state department cautions that these estimates do not guarantee an appointment within a specified period. Embassies and consulates release additional slots regularly, and applicants who have already scheduled interviews can check the appointment system for earlier dates.The published estimates also exclude appointments for applicants who qualify for an in-person interview waiver. Applicants are advised to check the relevant US embassy or consulate website for updated availability and appointment instructions.

items.title: SpaceX-Tesla merger: How to tackle China risk
items.summary: Elon Musk's potential mega-merger of Tesla and SpaceX would likely face a China-shaped hurdle from regulators on both sides of the Pacific over concerns about national security and the sharing of data and technology.The world's richest person said on Tuesday his two companies had set up special committees to discuss a union, calling a merger a "good idea". Turning it into reality, however, would mean navigating the thorny issue of Tesla's heavy reliance on China for manufacturing versus SpaceX's defence business.Rocket company SpaceX is increasingly reliant on sensitive US government and defence contracts, which could subject any merger involving Tesla's business in China to intense scrutiny on national security grounds.Also read: What to know about the Ebola outbreak that has spread from Congo to 4 other countriesChinese regulators also require Tesla to keep confidential user data collected by its automated driving systems firmly in China, and any firewall would have to prevent the flow of information or technology in either direction.Below are some ways that Musk and the companies could look to clear any barriers put up by Washington or Beijing.Could Tesla keep its China business?One potential option would be for the merged company to create a firewall around Tesla's Chinese operations to block access to sensitive data from SpaceX and other parts of the business. Such a move is not unheard of, said Daniel Kollar, head of automotive and mobility practice at consultancy Intralink Group.Plenty of companies have been able to run major defence businesses outside of China while maintaining operations in the country, he said, citing Airbus and Honeywell.Also read: Beyond the ballot: Why Israel's next leader may stick to Netanyahu's doctrineSpaceX's defence-related businesses include Starshield, which develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the Pentagon.A two-way firewall would also likely be the minimum requirement to ensure Tesla's data from Chinese drivers stays in China, analysts said. Since 2021, Tesla has been complying with Beijing's requirement to keep all driver data inside of China.Tesla could continue to operate in China for years to come as a self-contained unit with its own research and development and strict agreements to keep all data inside China, said Michael Dunne, CEO of automotive advisory firm Dunne Insights, which closely follows China's auto industry.Keeping both Beijing and Washington happy about such a firewall, however, could be tricky, said Christopher Tang, a professor at UCLA's Anderson School of Management who specializes in ​global supply chains. He said the Chinese government is likely to try to use any proposed merger to negotiate a range of items as a condition for approval."China will use it as leverage," Tang said. "They have the bargaining power right now."Ioannis Kokkoris, professor of competition law and economics at Queen Mary University of London, identified two possible concessions that China could seek: access for Chinese companies to strategically significant technologies, and commitments to retain manufacturing capacity and investment in China.Any demand to share sensitive SpaceX-related technology, however, would run directly into US security restrictions.What about divestment?Analysts have said there were likely three broad paths towards divestment: a spinoff in which Tesla retains a majority economic interest, a sale paired with long-term brand licensing agreements, or an outright sale, possibly to another automaker.Any kind of divestment would come with plenty of complications, including the looming question of who would buy the asset. China's automakers, which do not need any extra capacity, are unlikely to be interested, said Li Yanwei, an analyst at the China Automobile Dealers Association.Many foreign automakers, on the other hand, are already strapped for cash, making them unlikely buyers as well. Kollar said Musk would be more likely to sell the China operation off for parts rather than hand control to anyone else.But Kollar added that unless Musk wanted to signal a retreat from the auto business, he expected Tesla to find a way to retain its China operations under the existing ownership structure.Tesla China and China's State Administration of Market Regulation did not reply to requests for comment.China still needed for cash flowA clean break from China could be difficult. Chinese suppliers are deeply integrated in Musk's broader empire and Tesla's Shanghai production accounted for more than 50% of its global output, according to Yale Zhang, managing director at Shanghai-based consultancy AutoForesight.Some investors, though, say those considerations aren't big enough to get in the way of a deal.Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, a Tesla and SpaceX investor, said Tesla's China manufacturing base is considerable, but the electric vehicle maker has already been making moves to expand US production, particularly for humanoid robots and the Cybercab driverless car, and many investors are more focused on Musk's promises for where these are headed.Mulberry also said he thinks Tesla would argue to US regulators that its China operations wouldn't overlap with SpaceX, but if unsuccessful, he thinks Tesla could shut or scale back its China production."It's short-term enough and small enough to be digestible," he said.Tang, the UCLA professor, said that while Tesla's future prospects may lie outside of China, its current EV business is heavily reliant on it. Much of the cash needed to finance its future bets comes from China EV production, he said."That is exactly why China will take advantage of this moment," Tang said. "Because you still need them."

items.summary:
India has advised its nationals living in France and those travelling to the country to remain vigilant and exercise caution amid continuing unrest, violent clashes and localised curfews in parts of the European nation.
In an advisory issued on Wednesday, the Embassy of India in France urged Indian nationals to avoid large gatherings and crowded places where protests are taking place and follow instructions issued by local authorities.
"In view of the recent developments and localised curfews imposed in France, please remain vigilant and exercise due caution," it said.
The advisory comes as France grapples with widespread protests and riots, triggered by student demonstrations over high school conditions and expanding into mass anti-government anger over inflation and living costs. The unrest has been marked by incidents of looting, arson and clashes between demonstrators and police.
The Indian mission asked nationals to stay informed through local news reports and official updates

items.title: Crime Branch summons CJP's Saurav, Ashutosh
items.summary: New Delhi: Delhi Police Crime Branch has summoned Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office on Thursday.The development comes a day after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court ordered their release from judicial custody after accepting their personal and surety bonds and taking written undertakings from them to maintain peace and abide by the law.SEM Ritu Raj directed the two leaders to furnish personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each until the conclusion of the enquiry. The court also directed them to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.Also read: INDIA bloc leaders to hold online meeting on Thursday, roadmap for 'vote chori' protests on agendaIn their written undertakings, Das and Ranka promised not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also undertook not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future protests would be conducted within the constitutional framework."Further judicial custody does not appear to be necessary at this stage, particularly after written undertakings before this Court," the SEM court observed while ordering their release.The court directed the investigating officer to submit a verification report regarding the sureties at the next hearing. The matter has been listed for further proceedings on October 23 at 3 pm, with the two leaders and their sureties directed to remain present.Earlier, Delhi Police had sought a further three-day extension of their judicial custody, arguing that the apprehension of a breach of peace and law and order persisted. Police also cited alleged differences between statements made by the leaders before the court and their subsequent remarks to the media.Also read:'Will not take down Indian Flag': Priyanka Gandhi's son alleges 'protest' photos pulled down at Bikaner House exhibitionDuring the hearing, counsel for the two leaders tendered an unconditional apology to the court over the conduct cited by the police and assured that it would not be repeated.Das and Ranka were detained in connection with an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. The police had alleged that they entered the area through private premises and violated conditions relating to maintaining peace.The SEM court has clarified that the enquiry in the matter will continue in accordance with the law.
