items.summary: Authorities issued a red alert for Chennai, implying expectations of extremely heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours amid a vigourous northeast monsoon over Tamil Nadu. The Regional Meterological Centre in Chennai also issued an orange alert for surrounding areas, namely Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu and Thiruvallar districts. It was also issues for western districts of Theni, Coimbatore and Nilgiris.Also Read: Southwest monsoon exits India with 13% rain deficitThe red alert means a forecast of extremely heavy rainfall above 20 cm, and the orange alert means a forecast of very heavy rainfall above 11 cm.The issued bulleting said Saturday's upper air cyclonic circulation over the northern part of the state and south coastal Andhra Pradesh had become less marked.Despite this, Chennai and its neighbouring districts saw their first and heavy spell of rains. The weather report mentioned that Parry's Corner in Chennai received the highest rainfall. This was followed by Kathivakkam.The Greater Chennai Corporation said that pro-active field operations, constant rescue efforts and continued coordination made sure that major areas and subways did not face waterlogging amid severe weather conditions.A team from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and four teams from the Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force (TNDRF) were deployed on the ground to handle vulnerable areas. Nine relief centres were established, and food was being steadily distributed to residents.Also Read: India faces weakest monsoon in nearly two decades as El Nino strengthensRainwater has now been completely cleared from all major bus routes and streets. Pumping operations in remaining low-lying pockets were in final stages and would end shortly, thereby keeping the entire situation under control.Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and Minister for Public Works and Youth Welfare and Sports Development, Aadhav Arjuna, visited the Ripon Building, GCC headquarters, following heavy rainfall across the city and red alert.During his visit, Aadhav Arjuna met teams from NDRF and TNDRF deployed for rescue operations, held consultations, and issued necessary directives regarding rescue and relief measures.

The attack comes amid deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

Russia's Ministry of Defense said Sunday that its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, as well as the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea.

items.summary: In a historic step, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) will implement a major functional reorganisation of its administrative and operational structure from November 1 to strengthen specialised security management across critical infrastructure and strategic establishments nationwide.The reorganisation, approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), will realign the force's existing territorial sectors according to the specific security requirements of different industries and establishments, including power, coal, steel, petroleum and natural gas, ports, government buildings, museums, monuments and mass rapid transit systems.Under the revised structure, the force said, the National Capital Region Sector will be reorganised as the Government Building Museums and Monuments and Mass Rapid Transit System (GBMM & MRTS) Sector, New Delhi.The North Sector in New Delhi and North Eastern Sector-II in Kolkata will be restructured as the Power-I and Power-II Sectors, respectively. The Eastern Sector in Ranchi will become the Coal Sector, while the Central Sector in Bhilai will be converted into the Steel Sector.Similarly, the North Eastern Sector in Guwahati will become the Petroleum and Natural Gas Sector. The Western Sector in Mumbai and the South Sector in Chennai will be transformed into the West Coast Port Sector and East Coast Port Sector, respectively.The existing Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space (DAE & DoS) Sector in Bengaluru, Airport Sector-I in New Delhi and Airport Sector-II in Bengaluru will continue under their respective functional arrangements.The reorganisation, it said, aims to improve operational oversight, develop sector-specific expertise, ensure greater uniformity in security practices and strengthen coordination with the concerned ministries, departments and installation managements.The CISF provides security to a wide range of establishments, including airports, seaports, atomic energy and space installations, power plants, power grids, steel plants, coal mines, petroleum and natural gas facilities, currency note presses, government buildings, iconic monuments and mass transit systems.Each sector has distinct operational processes, infrastructure, potential hazards and security vulnerabilities, requiring specialised security arrangements.Under the earlier system, administrative and operational supervision was largely organised on the basis of territorial jurisdiction. Over the past 25 years, the force has progressively adopted a functional approach in selected sectors, including aviation and strategic establishments under the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space.The experience gained from this approach highlighted the advantages of specialised supervision, focused training, sector-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), better utilisation of specialised personnel and closer coordination with the concerned organisations.Building on this experience, the CISF reviewed the supervisory structure of the remaining territorial sectors and undertook the functional realignment following deliberations with supervisory formations, branches at force headquarters and senior officers, before obtaining MHA approval.The restructuring assumes significance as the CISF's mandate is expanding beyond conventional industrial security to cover new and specialised responsibilities.The force has been designated as a Recognised Security Organisation (RSO) for port facilities under the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code. The functional realignment of port-sector supervision is expected to support specialised port-security expertise and improve coordination with port authorities and other stakeholders.The CISF has also been entrusted with security responsibilities at high-security correctional facilities in Jammu and Kashmir and designated as the nodal agency for aerial security of critical infrastructure.The force is strengthening its cybersecurity and drone and anti-drone capabilities through specialised training and collaboration with premier institutions to improve preparedness against cyberattacks, digital threats and hostile unmanned aerial systems.The reorganisation is expected to establish a more specialised, sector-oriented security apparatus, improve operational accountability and strengthen protection of India's strategic and economic assets.

Instead of changing the court-fee system, the rules focus on administrative enforcement, accountability and time-bound conflict resolution.

items.title: Poor management, workplace culture key reasons behind job switch: Report
items.summary:
Career decisions are not driven by salary alone; rather, factors like poor management or workplace culture also play a key role for employees considering a job change, a report said on Sunday.
End-to-end workforce staffing and HR solutions provider Genius HRTech Limited's September 2026 report revealed that 47 per cent of respondents cited poor management or workplace culture as a key reason for considering a job change, while 30 per cent pointed to compensation below market expectations.
The Genius HRTech report is based on inputs from 1,255 employees during September 1-30 across sectors, including Information Technology (IT), manufacturing, telecom, retail, finance and BFSI, FMCG and engineering, among others.
Further, the report found that 39 per cent of respondents would be more likely to stay with their current employer if offered better management, a healthier workplace culture or greater flexibility.

items.title: Trivandrum airport halts flights on Tue
items.summary: Flight operations at Thiruvananthapuram International Airport will be suspended for five hours on October 20 to allow the traditional Arattu procession of Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple to pass across the runway.Thiruvananthapuram International Airport Ltd (TIAL) said on Sunday that flight services would remain suspended from 4 pm to 9 pm to facilitate the temple’s ‘Alpassi Arattu’ procession. Passengers have been advised to check revised flight timings with their respective airlines.Also read: Vietnam Airlines set to fly non-stop between Hanoi and Ahmedabad from November 2026The temporary suspension is part of a centuries-old tradition associated with the Travancore royal family. The procession takes the ceremonial idols of the temple to Shangumugham beach for a ritual holy bath before returning to the shrine.The airport has adjusted its operations twice a year for decades to accommodate the temple’s biannual Arattu processions. The practice continues despite the growth of the airport and changes in its management.The tradition dates back to the period of the erstwhile Travancore kingdom and has continued since the airport was established in 1932.Also read: Indian passport rises to 84th rank in Henley Passport Index 2026; visa-free access to 55 destinationsAccording to historians, the then Travancore king, Sree Chithira Thirunal, had stipulated that the airport would remain open to the public for 363 days a year, with the remaining two days reserved for Lord Padmanabha, the titular deity of the royal family.The ritual has continued even after the Adani Group took over the airport’s management. The runway crossing is a distinctive feature of the ceremony, reflecting the historical relationship between the temple, the former royal family and the airport. The temporary closure requires airlines to adjust their schedules to accommodate the procession.Passengers travelling to or from Thiruvananthapuram on October 20 should check with their airlines for updated departure and arrival times before heading to the airport.

The restriction, initially imposed on April 23, 2025, has been extended periodically since then amid strained relations between the two neighbouring countries.
The Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) announced the extension in a post on X on Saturday, saying the restriction also covers military flights.
The latest extension will remain in effect until 4:59 am (local time) on November 24, 2026, according to the authority.
A PAA spokesperson said a fresh Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued to extend the ban, Geo News reported.
Pakistan's airspace is divided into two flight information regions (FIRs) -- Karachi and Lahore, according to a Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) document from 2022. The latest NOTAM applies to both the Karachi and Lahore FIRs.

"This literally is the first time I've heard of this," Vance said in response.

items.title: Tata Trusts disbursed ₹1,556 crore in FY26, plans 40-50 nonprofit hospitals
items.summary:
Tata Trusts, India's largest philanthropic group, disbursed Rs 1,556.31 crore in the year to March 2026 and is now working toward a network of 40 to 50 not-for-profit general hospitals, Chairman Noel Tata said in the Trusts' Annual Report for 2025-26.
Tata said patients who can afford to pay would help fund care for those who cannot. The report gives no investment figure, locations, or timeline for the hospitals.
In his message, Tata said the Trusts want to build institutions and models that become "enduring public assets" and be judged on what changes as a result of their work. He wrote that measuring philanthropy by people reached or money spent is no longer enough.
Institutional grants and direct project spending came in at Rs 1,353.32 crore, and individual grants at  Rs 202.99 crore. Rural upliftment took the largest share at Rs 457.62 crore, followed by education (Rs 270.26 crore), cancer care (Rs 178.46 crore), institutions (Rs 169.31 crore) and healthcare (Rs 105.97 crore). .

"A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," Trump told reporters at the Mar-a-Lago resort in Miami on Saturday evening.
"It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world because we're really at a world stage," Trump said.

Higher output in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan will likely largely offset crop losses in Maharashtra, according to the association's first crop estimate report. The data was shared during the concluding session of SOPA's international soybean conference in Indore on Saturday.
Soybean is a key oilseed crop that provides domestic cooking oil and a protein base for the livestock and poultry industries.
Overall production is estimated to decline by 2.11 per cent from the previous season, the association said.

items.title: Japan to launch spacecraft on a mission to get samples from a Martian moon
items.summary:
Japan is set to launch a spacecraft on the world's first mission to bring back samples from Phobos, one of the two small, potato-shaped moons orbiting Mars.
Scientists hope the mission, which is expected to take five years, will provide clues to how Phobos and its smaller sibling Deimos formed, and hopefully even shed light on the origins of life in the solar system.
The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's launch of the spacecraft Tuesday on a new Japanese mainstay H-3 rocket comes as the United States, China and others consider sending astronauts to Mars.
Samples from Phobos will provide useful data for scientists to consider using a Martian moon as a base for a future manned mission to the planet, said MMX project manager Yasuhiro Kawakatsu.
"Despite their potential importance, Martian moons have never been fully investigated," Kawakatsu said. "They are known as the most important unclimbed mountains in the solar system."
